In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/8581):

>## What this PR does / why we need it:
>
>On KubeVirt, the bootstrap userdata Secret in the HCP namespace (`user-data-<nodepool>-<hash>`) is shared by all VMs in a given NodePool generation. During a rolling update, HyperShift's `secretJanitor` and `Token.cleanupOutdated()` eagerly delete the old userdata Secret as soon as a new config version is computed. Any VMs from the previous generation that are still running will then fail CAPK reconciliation because their referenced Secret no longer exists.
>
>This PR extends the existing AWS platform guard (which already preserves old userdata Secrets for a different reason) to also cover KubeVirt. With this change, old userdata Secrets are retained until the rollout finishes and old VMs are cleaned up.
>
>## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
>
>Fixes premature garbage collection of shared userdata Secrets on the KubeVirt provider during NodePool rolling updates.
>
>## Special notes for your reviewer:
>
>- The fix mirrors the existing AWS guard pattern. AWS preserves old userdata because of a CAPA bug (kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api-provider-aws#3805). KubeVirt needs it because the Secret is architecturally shared across VMs in a generation.
>- Long term, a more targeted cleanup (e.g. checking whether any old-generation VMs still reference the Secret) would be preferable, but this minimal change is safe and consistent with the existing pattern.
>

This PR extends the existing user-data Secret retention logic to support KubeVirt platform NodePools in addition to AWS. **Manual KubeVirt NodePool rolling update test**

Tested this PR by deploying a KubeVirt HostedCluster with a custom HyperShift operator image built from this branch, then triggering a NodePool rolling update and verifying that the old userdata Secret is preserved throughout the rollout.

**Environment**

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| Management cluster (OCP) | 4.20.0 |
| OpenShift Virtualization (CNV) | 4.20.15 |
| HyperShift operator | Built from commit `1edbe53df` (this PR, rebased on `main`) |
| CAPI KubeVirt provider | `quay.io/capk/capk-manager:v0.11.2` |
| HostedCluster release | `quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.22.3-multi` |
| NodePool replicas | 2 |
| Management cluster platform | AWS (bare-metal compute nodes for KVM support) |

**Test procedure**

1. Provisioned an OCP 4.20 management cluster with bare-metal worker nodes.
2. Installed OpenShift Virtualization (CNV) operator.
3. Built a custom HyperShift operator image from this PR branch and deployed it.
4. Created a KubeVirt HostedCluster with a 2-replica NodePool (RollingUpdate strategy, maxSurge=1, maxUnavailable=0).
5. Waited for both guest nodes to reach `Ready` state.
6. Recorded the pre-rollout userdata Secret: `user-data-rollout-test-33491014-userdata`.
7. Triggered a rolling update by changing `spec.platform.kubevirt.compute.cores` from 2 to 4.
8. Monitored the rollout through completion.

**Results: PASS**

The rolling update completed successfully with no errors:

- **Surge machine created**: a new machine with the updated VM spec was provisioned and reached `Running`/`Ready`.
- **Old userdata Secret preserved during rollout**: `user-data-rollout-test-33491014-userdata` was retained while old machines were being deleted. This is the behaviour fixed by this PR.
- **Old machines deleted cleanly**: both original machines entered `Deleting` phase and were fully removed without reconciliation errors.
- **Second replacement machine provisioned**: the second new machine was created, booted, and joined the guest cluster.
- **Final state**: 2/2 new machines `Running`/`Ready`/`UP-TO-DATE`, NodePool stable, no errors in operator logs.

**Key observation (the fix in action)**

During the rollout, the old userdata Secret was preserved because:
- `token.go` / `cleanupOutdated`: the condition `t.nodePool.Spec.Platform.Type != hyperv1.KubevirtPlatform` prevented premature deletion of the old userdata Secret.
- `secret_janitor.go` / `shouldKeepOldUserData`: the early return for `KubevirtPlatform` ensured the secret janitor also retained it.

Without this PR, the old userdata Secret would have been garbage collected while old VMs still referenced it, causing machine deletion failures during the rollout.

Thanks for the fix, the approach is sound and consistent with the existing pattern.

One ask: could you please create a Jira ticket to track making the secret retention rollout-aware? Right now both AWS and KubeVirt keep the old userdata Secret unconditionally for the platform — ideally cleanup would check whether any old-generation VMs/Machines still reference the Secret and delete it once they are gone. That would be a nice follow-up for both platforms. We would like to have the ticket so we can discuss scope and priority in our scrum.

>## What this PR does / why we need it:
>
>On KubeVirt, the bootstrap userdata Secret in the HCP namespace (`user-data-<nodepool>-<hash>`) is shared by all VMs in a given NodePool generation. During a rolling update, HyperShift's `secretJanitor` and `Token.cleanupOutdated()` eagerly delete the old userdata Secret as soon as a new config version is computed. Any VMs from the previous generation that are still running will then fail CAPK reconciliation because their referenced Secret no longer exists.
>
>This PR extends the existing AWS platform guard (which already preserves old userdata Secrets for a different reason) to also cover KubeVirt. With this change, old userdata Secrets are retained until the rollout finishes and old VMs are cleaned up.
>
>## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
>
>Fixes premature garbage collection of shared userdata Secrets on the KubeVirt provider during NodePool rolling updates.
>
>## Special notes for your reviewer:
>
>- The fix mirrors the existing AWS guard pattern. AWS preserves old userdata because of a CAPA bug (kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api-provider-aws#3805). KubeVirt needs it because the Secret is architecturally shared across VMs in a generation.
>- Long term, a more targeted cleanup (e.g. checking whether any old-generation VMs still reference the Secret) would be preferable, but this minimal change is safe and consistent with the existing pattern.
>
>## Manual testing
>
>Verified on a real KubeVirt HostedCluster (OCP 4.20 management cluster with CNV 4.20.15, guest release 4.22.3, 2-replica NodePool). Triggered a rolling update by changing VM compute cores. The old userdata Secret was preserved throughout the rollout, both old machines were deleted cleanly, and the rollout completed with no errors. Full test evidence: https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/8581#issuecomment-4809162171
